topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the stepwise accumulation of cellular changes as a model of cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer as disrupted differentiation and tissue organisation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why cancer must be understood in the context of organised tissues rather than through isolated tumour cells alone.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign tumours from invasive and metastatic malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish invasion and spread as defining features of malignancy and show how those features are recognised in tumour specimens.

topics.label: Benign tumours and progression to invasive cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine progression from benign growth to invasive malignancy while qualifying what benign status means for a patient's risk.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names convey tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming rules.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth and metastatic spread impair normal bodily function and can become lethal.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine why early cancer detection is difficult and what makes screening effective or limited in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by directing students back to the learning outcomes and ahead to revision and practical teaching.
